first.rationale: Activation and onboarding are both declining, so simplifying onboarding directly addresses the most immediate funnel constraint and may improve time-to-value without conceding margin to the competitor. I will verify the prior onboarding and signup experiments before committing, while guarding against downstream risks such as lower-quality signups or weaker qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a small guarded test of shortened onboarding, prioritizing the direct response to the 4% decline in completion and 6% decline in activation. The verified result showed a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention. Because signup simplification reduced retention by 1% despite improving qualified revenue by 4% and only held for SMBs, monitor qualified revenue, lead quality, and retention by segment before expanding.

final2.rationale: The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-sensitive SMB churn create an immediate revenue risk that now outweighs the onboarding opportunity for this cycle. Test targeted, time-limited promotional pricing only for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB prospects and at-risk accounts, with holdouts and safeguards against margin erosion, cannibalization, low-quality acquisition, and retention decline. Expand only if qualified revenue and retained gross profit improve, not merely conversion.
